[Video 1](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html). ## [](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html)A missing dot. Heading into the meeting, Fed watchers had suspected [Warsh wouldn’t submit his outlook](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/16/fed-chair-warsh-expected-to-withhold-dot-from-central-banks-interest-rate-outlook.html), and some anticipated he might look to end the feature altogether. He confirmed at [a news conference](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-meeting-today-live-updates.html) following the decision that he had declined to share a forecast and is forming task forces to overhaul major Fed operations. ## [](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html)A shorter statement. In addition to the rate call, which was widely anticipated in financial markets, the [FOMC’s post-meeting statement](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/june-fed-meeting-redline.html) also not only removed prior language seen as a nod toward an easing slant in the future but took a hatchet to the rest of it. ## [](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html)Higher inflation forecast. Nonfarm payroll growth again [defied expectations in May](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/05/jobs-report-may-2026.html) with a gain of 172,000 while the unemployment rate, the Fed’s most closely watched metric, was at 4.3%, unchanged over the past year. *   ![Image 14: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) Opt-Out Icon](https://static-redesign.cnbcfm.com/dist/17269f1b6083fd5f61be.svg)[Your Privacy Choices](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html).
